dedupe_keys.name: california fire stations seismic risk assessment and retrofit benefit cost study phase i seismic safety commission 2025

description: This case study is the California Seismic Safety Commission's Phase I study of earthquake risk to fire stations and of whether retrofitting them pays off. Working with Cal OES, the Commission ran FEMA's HAZUS Advanced Engineering Building Module and the FEMA BCA Toolkit on sample fire station buildings, mainly reinforced masonry and wood types, and compared the benefit-to-cost ratios of upgrading them from Moderate Code to High Code or Special High Code. The BCA Toolkit, updated in 2023, often gave higher ratios than HAZUS. Counting loss of function, which matters because most California fire calls are medical, raised the benefits a lot, while contents losses are missed by the toolkit. The report also documents jammed roll-up doors after the 2022 Ferndale earthquake, which delayed an engine at Rio Dell by about twenty minutes, and asks for a performance standard and early-warning-triggered door openers. The 55-page report is free to download as a PDF. Coverage is California; Phase I uses HAZUS default building data, and a Phase II based on a statewide voluntary survey of stations is under way. Caveats: results are for sample building types, not an inventory of every station, and no licence is stated. Simulation uses: prioritising retrofits and putting a value on lost emergency service in seismic loss models. Related records: the Oregon rapid visual screening data (data-oregon-statewide-seismic-needs-assessment-rvs) give building-level inputs for a similar analysis.

outcomes: Compares benefit-to-cost ratios of retrofitting fire stations from Moderate Code to High Code or Special High Code with HAZUS AEBM and the FEMA BCA Toolkit; the BCA Toolkit often gives higher ratios; including loss of function, especially for stations providing emergency medical services, markedly raises benefits; loss of contents is not captured in the BCA Toolkit; stuck roll-up doors (Rio Dell, 2022 Ferndale earthquake, about 20 minutes' delay) are flagged as an unregulated vulnerability.
